tool.name: SimpleHypsometricShading
tool.summary: Creates a group layer that drapes a DEM (black-to-white stretch at a chosen transparency) over an existing hillshade for classic hypsometric (elevation-tinted) relief. No new dataset is created; the group layer references the existing rasters and remains fully editable.
tool.usage:
Hypsometric shading adds an impression of overall elevation to a hillshade: low terrain darkens toward black while high terrain stays bright. Rather than baking that effect into a new raster, this tool simply composes a group layer from two rasters you already have - the DEM on top, symbolized with a minimum-to-maximum black-to-white stretch (black at the lowest elevation) and set to the transparency you choose, over your existing hillshade beneath. Because the result is ordinary layers, everything stays freely editable afterward: swap the color ramp for a terrain ramp, adjust the transparency slider, change the stretch, choose a different layer blend mode, or reorder the layers.
The DEM layer can also be given any of ArcGIS Pro's layer blend modes, which control how it combines with the hillshade beneath: Normal, Multiply, Darken, and Luminosity often work well for hypsometric shading. The blend mode is an ordinary layer property, so it is easy to change manually after the group layer is created (select the DEM layer, then use Layer Blend on the Raster Layer ribbon tab).
Both inputs can be chosen from the layers in your map or browsed from disk. The hillshade can come from any source - the Enhanced, MDOW, or Multi-Sun Hillshade tools, Esri's own hillshade, or any raster you want beneath the elevation tint.
This tool is one part of the classic "Swiss style" of relief presentation (after Eduard Imhof and the Swiss cartographers, whose hand-drawn conventions Kurt Brassel first automated), which combines three strategies: illuminating the terrain from multiple directions, elevation-based tone adjustments that mimic atmospheric perspective, and softening of the final image. In this toolbox the MDOW Hillshade and Multi-Sun Hillshade tools provide the multi-directional illumination, the hypsometric-shading options and the Simple Hypsometric Shading tool provide the elevation-based tinting, and the Blurred Hillshade tool provides the softening.
No new dataset is created and no geoprocessing environments apply: the tool writes only a small layer file in the scratch folder that references the two existing rasters, and returns it as the output group layer (added to your map automatically when "Add output datasets to an open map" is enabled in the geoprocessing options). The last-used transparency is remembered with the project.
Tip: the same effect at full control is available inside the Enhanced and Multi-Sun Hillshade tools as the "Apply hypsometric shading" option, which bakes the darkening into the output raster; use this tool when you prefer a live, adjustable layer arrangement instead.

dialogReference.para: The elevation raster (DEM) to drape over the hillshade. It must be single band. Choose a raster from the map or browse to one on disk.
The existing hillshade raster to sit beneath the elevation tint. Choose a raster from the map or browse to one on disk.

The transparency applied to the whole DEM layer, 0 (opaque - the hillshade is hidden) to 100 (invisible - only the hillshade shows). The default 50 gives an even blend; adjust the layer's transparency slider afterward to taste.

How the DEM layer blends with the hillshade beneath it, using ArcGIS Pro's standard layer blend modes. Normal, Multiply, Darken, and Luminosity often work well for hypsometric shading. You can easily change the blend mode manually after the group layer is created: select the DEM layer and use Layer Blend on the Raster Layer ribbon tab.
The name of the group layer added to the map. A suggested name is filled in from the DEM.
The composed group layer: the symbolized DEM over the hillshade. It references the existing rasters; no new dataset is created.

scriptExample.title: Simple Hypsometric Shading example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Compose the group layer and save it permanently with SaveToLayerFile if desired.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your installed path is shown in this tool's run messages result = arcpy.jenness.SimpleHypsometricShading( in_dem=r"C:\Project\Elev.gdb\DEM", in_hillshade=r"C:\Project\Elev.gdb\DEM_Hillshade", transparency=50, group_name="DEM Hypsometric Shading") print(result.getOutput(0)) # path to the composed group .lyrx

dataIdInfo.idPurp: Group-layer composition for hypsometric (elevation-tinted) relief: DEM stretched black-to-white at a chosen transparency over an existing hillshade; creates no new dataset.
dataIdInfo.idAbs: Creates a group layer that drapes a DEM over an existing hillshade for a classic hypsometric-shading effect: the DEM is symbolized with a black-to-white minimum-to-maximum stretch (black at the lowest elevation) and set to a user-chosen transparency, on top of the hillshade. No new dataset is created - the tool writes a small layer file referencing the two existing rasters and returns it as a group layer, so the arrangement (ramp, transparency, stretch, layer order) remains freely editable in the map. Inputs can be map layers or datasets browsed from disk.
